archetype.name: Game Manager (backup)
archetype.definition: An undrafted, short-area distributor who keeps the offense on schedule with completions underneath but has no reliable answer when the throw has to travel past the sticks.

report.headline: A competent checkdown backup whose floor collapses once he pushes past ten yards
report.take:
Tyson Bagent is Chicago's QB2. Caleb Williams has started every game since Week 6, and Bagent's 2026 consists of a relief cameo against Minnesota, a full game against the Jets and one start at Green Bay. That's 70 dropbacks. Everything below is a read on a backup's toolkit, not a full-season profile. The toolkit looks a lot like his 2023 rookie year. He threw short then (6.2 aDOT, a 65.7% completion rate), and he throws short now: intended air yards of 6.02, and he throws 1.93 yards short of the sticks on average.

The short game is real. On throws of 0-9 air yards he's completing 72.4% at +0.175 EPA with a 62% success rate. That's the Ben Johnson offense working as designed, with quick, defined reads and timing throws in the middle of the field. The damage comes in the 10-19 yard window. He's 41.2% there with a -13.8 CPOE, and all three of his interceptions came on those throws. That one band is why a 65.6% passer with a positive CPOE sits 47th in adjusted net yards per dropback and 48th in interception rate.

The game log shows how dependent he is on the matchup. Against the Jets, whose defense now ranks 30th, he went 25/34 for 268 and +7.0 EPA in a 23-12 win. At Green Bay, a top-10 defense, he went 12/21 for 87 with two interceptions, a 23.8% bad-throw rate and -8.6 EPA in a 7-31 loss. Against a soft defense with a clean pocket he can run the offense. Against a good one the windows tighten, he forces intermediate throws, and it unravels. The red zone (-0.326 EPA, no touchdowns) and under-center snaps (-0.239) point the same way. When the field shrinks or the play-action shot has to be hit, he doesn't find answers.

The target split fits. Rome Odunze has been a +0.506 EPA-per-target outlet for him. Colston Loveland, at -0.453 per target, is where the drives died, probably because the tight end is the one working those intermediate seams. A few of these numbers are small-sample noise: five deep attempts, a 40% pressure-to-sack rate that clashes with his excellent 2023 mark. The overall shape is consistent across both seasons, though. He is a functional caretaker who needs the opponent to cooperate.

strengths.title: Accurate, efficient underneath game
strengths.body: Throws inside 10 air yards are the core of his game. He completes them at a high rate with positive EPA and a strong success rate, which is what keeps a Johnson offense on schedule with him in. It's a skill he showed as a rookie too (18th in success rate in 2023), so it should hold whenever he plays.

strengths.title: Can run the offense versus weak defenses
strengths.body: The Jets game showed his ceiling: 268 yards and +7.0 EPA against a defense that now ranks 30th, with almost no pressure. When the protection holds and the coverage is soft, the quick game piles up yards. That conditional ceiling matters for a team that would only use him in an emergency.

concerns.title: Intermediate throws produce the turnovers
concerns.body: All three interceptions came on 10-19 yard throws, where his accuracy falls apart. These are the throws that test anticipation and arm talent rather than reading a defined route. It's a genuine limitation rather than bad luck, and it's why his interception rate sits near the bottom of the league.

concerns.title: Collapses against quality defenses
concerns.body: His lone start, at Green Bay, produced -8.6 EPA, a -10.9 CPOE and a 23.8% bad-throw rate. Combined with the 3-point relief outing against the top-ranked Vikings, the pattern is clear. Good defenses take away the underneath stuff, and he has no second gear. His -0.374 EPA per dropback as a starter is a one-game sample, but it fits that pattern.

concerns.title: No finishing in the red zone
concerns.body: He's 46.7% with no touchdowns and -0.326 EPA in the red zone, and has zero passing touchdowns overall. A condensed field punishes a passer who relies on space underneath. The touchdown rate will tick up with more volume, but the compressed-field problem fits his profile.

trend.note: His three appearances swung from a modest relief outing against Minnesota to +7.0 EPA against the Jets to -8.6 at Green Bay, tracking almost entirely with the quality of the defense. He hasn't taken a meaningful snap since Williams returned in Week 6.

nextGame.headline: Soft Saints defense, but he's the QB2 behind Williams
nextGame.body:
On paper this is the kind of defense Bagent can operate against. New Orleans ranks 23rd in defensive EPA, 20th against the pass and 22nd on short throws, the area where his game lives. The catch is that he's listed as QB2 behind Caleb Williams, who has started every game since Week 6. Barring a change at the top of the depth chart, Bagent's involvement depends on game script. Chicago is an 11.5-point favorite, so mop-up snaps in a blowout are the realistic scenario, and those tend to be handoffs and quick throws rather than stat-padding drives.

Availability: the Bears lost left tackle Braxton Jones (65% of snaps) for the season, which weakens the protection for any QB. Luther Burden III, his co-leader in targets, is questionable with a concussion but practiced Monday. On the Saints' side, the injuries are mostly on offense (both tackles and the center out). That helps Chicago build the kind of lead that brings the backup in. The forecast shows sustained wind around 16 mph with gusts near 26, though it's early. If it holds, it favors a run-heavy fourth quarter even more.

keyMatchups.title: Blowout script decides his snaps
keyMatchups.body: A double-digit spread and a -650 moneyline make this the most likely type of game for a backup to see the field. Any late series would probably be run-first and conservative, especially if the wind holds up.

keyMatchups.title: Saints' weak short-area coverage
keyMatchups.body: New Orleans gives up positive EPA on short throws and ranks near the bottom on deep passes. That's the same soft profile the Jets presented in his best game. If he does throw, his quick game should find completions.

keyMatchups.title: Saints pass rush vs. thinner line
keyMatchups.body: The Saints rank 5th in sack rate, and the Bears are without Jones. Bagent's pressure-to-sack rate this season has been poor on a small sample, so even brief action carries sack risk.

nextGame.watch: Whether Williams is on the final injury report. Without that, Bagent's only route to snaps is a fourth-quarter blowout.

restOfSeason.body:
As long as Williams is healthy, Bagent's rest of season is clipboard duty plus the occasional garbage-time series. Expect near-zero production in most weeks. His useful skill, accurate short passing, is real and has held across two seasons. So is the intermediate-throw problem that produces his interceptions. Neither will show up much in mop-up duty.

If he's forced into starts, expect the Jets-or-Packers split to repeat. A soft defense with clean pockets should yield a serviceable 180-220 yards with few explosives. A good defense likely means sub-150 yards and turnover risk. The zero-touchdown mark will regress with volume, but his touchdown and red-zone profile suggests he'd stay below average there. The interception rate should also drift down from its current level, though not to league average.
swingFactors: Strength of opposing defense in any spot start

confidence.note: 70 dropbacks across three uneven appearances; backup role makes playing time unpredictable.
